messages:
Maria Chen: heads up — eu-central-1c egress has had repeated packet loss to the gpu pools for ~10m, p95 latency spikes, and a few failed healthchecks on kube-proxy. seen in net-monitor and gpu-fleet dashboards. :rotating_light:
ops-bot: alert: net-monitor detected interface error rate > 5% on eu-central-1c (since 2025-11-29T09:14:00Z)
Ajay Patel: ack. can we confirm scope? is it just egress network path or whole AZ?
Maria Chen: looks like external egress (NAT/IGW) paths to that AZ. internal pod-to-pod seems ok. but GPUs report retransmits and some oomc failures due to lost control msgs.
Leo Gomez: rough capacity in 1c right now is 120 active GPU units, 30% reserved for batch. 1a/1b have ~40 spare units each. we can spillover but need to ensure throughput for live routes.
Sophie Park: if we start draining nodes in 1c we should do it in waves — don't want large cache/KV warmup on other zones.
Ajay Patel: agree. propose cordon+drain low-priority batch nodes first, then route serving traffic away from 1c via routing policy update.
Maria Chen: plan: 1) cordon batch nodes in 1c (non-critical) 2) update smart-routing to prefer 1a/1b for serving 3) scale up warm pool in 1a by +4 GPUs as cushion 4) start controlled node drains of leftover instances 5) monitor quality/regressions
Leo Gomez: fine, add throttling to rollout: max 2 nodes drained concurrently. also set cache-prefetch window to 15s to reduce cold starts.
Ajay Patel: commands I'm running now:
```bash
kubectl get nodes -l topology.kubernetes.io/zone=eu-central-1c -o name | grep gpu | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl cordon {}
kubectl drain gpu-1c-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --force
```
Maria Chen: I'm flipping the routing policy to prefer zones 1a/1b with a 10% gradual shift, not instantaneous. updating config: `redwood-routing update --region eu-central-1 --bias 1a=0.55,1b=0.45,1c=0.0 --strategy gradual --step 10`
Sophie Park: remind me — do we have autoscaler overrides for warm pool?
Leo Gomez: yes, using infra cli: `rdm infra scale --pool gpu-warm --region eu-central-1a --count +4 --type on-demand` to avoid reserved commit changes.
Ajay Patel: started cordoning 3 batch nodes (gpu-1c-05..07). draining should finish in ~6min each.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout job queued: routing-policy-update-1759004321 by Maria Chen — step=1/10
Maria Chen: noticing fewer healthcheck failures after first drain and routing step. p50 latency down ~30ms.
Sophie Park: cost check — scaling warm pool on-demand will add ~0.6x hourly cost short-term, but prevents failed requests. agree to proceed for 2 hours then reassess.
Leo Gomez: I'll keep the concurrent drains at 2 and hold back pool autoscaler from autoscaling down for 30m after traffic stabilizes.
Ajay Patel: drain of gpu-1c-07 complete, pods rescheduled to 1a/1b. no evictions for priorityClass=serve-high.
Maria Chen: starting next phase: cordon remaining non-critical nodes, then we'll decide about draining any critical serving nodes if errors persist.
Leo Gomez: if egress path doesn't recover in 30m, we should consider cross-region failover for heavy jobs (asia will be bad latency but avoids tail failures). keep that as last resort.
Sophie Park: logging this incident as intermittent AZ egress flap. I'll create an incident ticket and link traffic graphs once we stabilize.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-20251129-az-egress-flap by Sophie Park
Ajay Patel: updating thread — all low-priority batch nodes in 1c cordoned+drained. routing bias at step 4/10, traffic moved ~35%. ongoing monitoring.
Maria Chen: good work. next check in 15m to decide further drains or rollback. :thumbsup:
